## Solution

**Step 1: Determine $f(x)$.**

The condition "$|f(x)| > \tfrac12$ has no solutions in $[1,3]$" means $|f(x)|\le \tfrac12$ for all $x\in[1,3]$. For the requested iterated value to be uniquely determined, $f$ must be the **extremal** quadratic — the monic quadratic of *minimal* sup-norm on $[1,3]$, which attains the bound $\tfrac12$ (equioscillation). This is the shifted Chebyshev polynomial.

Set $t = x-2\in[-1,1]$. Then
$$f(x)=x^{2}+px+q=(t+2)^{2}+p(t+2)+q=t^{2}+(4+p)t+(4+2p+q).$$

The monic quadratic of minimal sup-norm on $[-1,1]$ is $t^{2}-\tfrac12$ (i.e. $\tfrac12 T_{2}(t)$), with sup-norm exactly $\tfrac12$. Equating coefficients:
$$4+p=0,\qquad 4+2p+q=-\tfrac12 \;\Longrightarrow\; p=-4,\; q=\tfrac72.$$

Hence
$$\boxed{f(x)=(x-2)^{2}-\tfrac12}.$$

**Verification:** $f(1)=\tfrac12,\; f(2)=-\tfrac12,\; f(3)=\tfrac12$, so $|f(x)|\le\tfrac12$ on $[1,3]$ with equioscillation at three points. ✓

**Step 2: Iterate from $a_{0}=\dfrac{3+\sqrt7}{2}$.**

Define $a_{n+1}=f(a_{n})$.

$$a_{1}=f(a_{0})=(a_{0}-2)^{2}-\tfrac12=\left(\frac{\sqrt7-1}{2}\right)^{2}-\tfrac12=\frac{8-2\sqrt7}{4}-\tfrac12=\frac{3-\sqrt7}{2}.$$

$$a_{2}=f(a_{1})=(a_{1}-2)^{2}-\tfrac12=\left(\frac{-1-\sqrt7}{2}\right)^{2}-\tfrac12=\frac{8+2\sqrt7}{4}-\tfrac12=\frac{3+\sqrt7}{2}=a_{0}.$$

So the orbit is **periodic with period 2**:
$$a_{0}\;\to\;a_{1}\;\to\;a_{0}\;\to\;a_{1}\;\to\;\cdots$$

Since $2017$ is **odd**, $a_{2017}=a_{1}$.

**Step 3: Compute the value.**

$$f^{2017}\!\left(\frac{3+\sqrt7}{2}\right)=\frac{3-\sqrt7}{2}\approx\frac{3-2.64575}{2}\approx 0.17712.$$

Rounded to the nearest hundredth:

$$\boxed{0.18}$$
